sections.content: Pack size, mostly. A 30ml serum and a six-piece kit are not the same product at different prices, and the gap between them is roughly what the ingredients cost.

The second thing is the active ingredient. Vitamin C, retinol and hyaluronic acid each cost the manufacturer real money. A cream that lists ceramides near the top of the ingredients and a cream that lists fragrance first are both called moisturiser and are not the same purchase.
The third thing, and the one nobody puts in the table, is where it came from.

sections.text: A Rs. 934 serum and a Rs. 6,000 serum are not the same product

sections.content: This is the part that matters more than any price in the table above.

Imported CeraVe in Pakistan, bought from the official distributor, costs several times what we charge. That gap is not us being generous. It is a different supply chain, and you should know which one is in front of you before you decide what's fair.

Branded skincare is one of the most copied categories in this market. Sellers know it, buyers suspect it, and almost nobody says it out loud. So here it is plainly: if a price is a fraction of what the brand's own website charges, it is worth asking why before you buy, from us or from anyone.
Three things to check on any tube, wherever you buy it:

items: The batch and expiry codes should be printed clearly, not stickered over
The packaging print should be sharp — smudged text is a bad sign on any brand
The texture should match the product. A serum should not feel like lotion

sections.content: If you need the imported original with a distributor guarantee, buy it from a pharmacy or the official retailer and pay the real price. We cannot give you that guarantee, so we won't pretend to.

sections.text: Don't buy CeraVe from us if…

sections.content: You have a skin condition that a dermatologist is treating. A Rs. 900 serum is not a substitute for a prescription, and a retinol at any price will make an active flare-up worse. Ask your doctor first. We'll still be here afterwards.
You're buying it as a gift for someone who uses only imported products. They will notice, and you will have bought a present that creates a conversation you don't want to have.
You want a guarantee that it is the global formulation. We can't verify that for you. What we can do is deliver it, let you open it before you pay, and take it back for seven days if it's not right.

sections.text: How to build a routine for under Rs. 1,000 here

sections.content: Cleanser and one active. That's it. That's the routine.

The Hydrating Skin Polish at Rs. 604 and the Vitamin C Serum at Rs. 934 come to Rs. 1,538 together. Or pick the Renewing SA Cleanser duo at Rs. 1,046 if you have oily skin and want salicylic acid in the wash instead of a serum.
Everything above that is optional. Serums add up quickly because each one promises a different result, and a shelf full of half-used serums is one of the most expensive things in your bathroom.

We cannot verify the authenticity of branded skincare for you, and we will not claim to. What we offer is the price, cash on delivery so you can inspect before paying, and a 7-day return window. Check the batch code and packaging as you would with any branded product.

items.q: How do I know which CeraVe serum to start with?
items.a: Vitamin C is the safer first serum for most people. Retinol needs a slower introduction and a sunscreen habit. Hyaluronic acid is mostly for dryness and will not change texture the way the other two can.

sections.content: The most expensive skincare product is the one you buy twice because the first one wasn't what you thought. Check the batch code, start with one active, and give it six weeks before deciding it doesn't work. If you'd rather we didn't sell it to you at all, that's a fine outcome too — we'd rather you kept the Rs. 900 and came back when you know what you need.
